newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends higher, close seen positive.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends higher, close seen positive.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled near the day's highs, buoyed by late-session speculative buying and interest from Far Eastern dealers in the March/May spread, floor sources said.
They viewed the settlement as bullish for prices, citing a close near the day's highs despite the week's low of 10.75 cents hit early in the session.
The May contract ended at a 0.01 cent premium to March compared with a 0.03 cent premium on Tuesday.
The most-active contract closed 0.06 cent higher at 10.89, having ranged form 10.91 to 10.75 cents. March settled up 0.10 cent to 10.90.
Volume was estimated at 24,118 lots compared with Tuesday's official volume of 25,262 lots.
Open interest in the March contract fell 6,087 lots to 11,211 lots as of the close Tuesday. Friday is the last trading day for March sugar.

The market opened down on follow-through selling, hitting the day's low of 10.75 cents basis May in early trade. Producer buying and short-covering lifted the most-active month over unchanged, where speculative buying emerged to carry prices to the highs, dealers said.
They said the market will turn its attention from the spread to the May contract, pegging nearby resistance just over today's high, at 10.92 cents.
Support was seen at 10.72 cents in May.
